instagram_reel.script:
Grenache is overdue for its moment. It’s one of the most widely planted red grapes in the world, but so many people still overlook it.

What makes it so good? It’s soft, round, and really food-friendly. You’ll often get ripe red fruit, some herbs, and this warm, spicy finish that makes it so easy to love.

And it’s not just one thing. Grenache shows up in big blends, beautiful rosé, and even white wine. So if you think you know Grenache, there’s a good chance there’s more to it.

linkedin.post:
Grenache is one of the most widely planted red grapes in the world, yet it still doesn’t get the attention it deserves.

That’s surprising, because it offers something the wine trade is always trying to communicate: versatility. Grenache can be approachable and generous in youth, but it also has the structure and complexity to shine in serious wines and classic blends.

It’s also a great reminder that origin and context matter. From the Southern Rhône to Priorat, Barossa, Sardinia, and beyond, Grenache shows how dramatically site and climate shape style.

For trade partners and buyers, that makes it a strong grape to recommend across multiple occasions: easygoing reds, rosé, blends, and even white wine expressions.

It’s a grape with range, and that’s part of what makes it so valuable.

quote_card: Grenache is the one you didn’t notice at first, and then couldn’t stop talking to all night.
